issues.title: Action Page - Service Requirement breadcrumb link
issues.description:
On Action pages, the breadcrumb link to the associated Service Requirement points to `/service-requirements/details/0`, when it should point to `/service-requirements/details/nnn`, where `nnn` represents the ID of the service requirement.

issues.title: Milestone Status Report Reflecting Incorrect Information
issues.description: The Milestone Status Report is showing incorrect information, based on the report itself it's displaying the Initial / Revised dates, this should be showing the completed dates for milestones that have been finalized, and the most current projected date for milestones that are still in-progress.

issues.title: Mod-Decr Value Not Allowing to Input a Negative Number
issues.description: Whenever inputting a descope value, it's not allowing to modify the already existing number as a negative number. For instance, if the action already had -50,000, but it needs to be changed to -55,000, it's not allowing the -55,000 to be added - only allowing a positive number. This is also reflecting on the dashboard as a positive number instead of a negative.

issues.title: bug: Duplicated records in Service Requirements screen
issues.description:
From issue tracker:
> There are at least 5 employee badge/PKI service requirements listed in the Service Requirements view, 2 PSDR, 2 RSS, and possible other duplicates

**Notes**
As noted in the issue tracker item, this affects some Service Requirements entries but not all. For those that it does affect, it appears that a copy of the Service Requirement item is added to the list any time that Service Requirement is clicked on from the screen and opened. 

For example, if you click on the "RSS" item on the Service Requirements screen and then navigate back to the Service Requirements screen, you will see an additional copy of the RSS item. (Same for the others that are exhibiting this behavior.)

This is happening on both TEST and PROD. I have not confirmed if it is affecting all the same items on each. I have not done any research to determine commonalities among the affected items nor differences with the unaffected items.
